opening_message:
Ticket 1: Casey Wu (employee ID E005) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E005.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Casey Wu (E005), full-time Payroll Specialist, requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access; write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E005 (Casey Wu) as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read access; write is not permitted. Recommend granting read for Source Code (requested write exceeds policy).
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists Casey Wu as full-time, but the Security DB lists E005 as a contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training caps access at read. Since the requested write access exceeds the contractor maximum, I grant the maximum permitted level of read. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Casey is a Payroll Specialist, so admin is not applicable in any case. Because the security database is the authoritative source for access-relevant status and the safest reading of policy, I grant read.

2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. Casey is a Payroll Specialist, so even as full-time, admin wouldn't be allowed, but write is allowed for full-time.

If contractor with basic training: max read.
